item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-7f5bbc2fd34c5183","start_unit":8,"end_unit":9,"fact_summary":"On June 7, 2023, Hasina told parliament that the World Bank had recognized its corruption allegations concerning the Padma Bridge project as false; she said she had expressed resentment to the Bank and would not patronize purposes diminishing Bangladesh’s dignity. She also reported food stocks, procurement and imports intended to support food security, and said Bangladesh was pursuing a CEPA with India in response to anticipated post-LDC export disadvantages.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.3","5B.7","5B.9","5B.10","6B.2","6B.6","7B.1","7B.2","8B.1","8B.2","8B.6","8B.7","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly concerns 2023 parliamentary statements and reported 2023 food-security and trade measures; claims of World Bank recognition are Hasina’s account as reported, not independently verified here.","ruler_attribution":"Hasina as prime minister and parliamentary leader reported policies, targets, and her response to the World Bank.","limitations":["The documents do not independently verify the World Bank’s position, the effectiveness of the food-security measures, or the projected CEPA effects."]},{"source_id":"SRC-79247c52c8aa31d2","start_unit":7,"end_unit":7,"fact_summary":"On January 14, 2023, Hasina said the Awami League always fulfills election pledges and that her government worked according to its pledges; she attributed reduced poverty, employment, rural freelancing, planned export diversification and investment in 100 economic zones to government policy, while saying she would act on information about corruption.","question_ids":["4B.2","5B.1","5B.4","5B.5","5B.6","5B.7","5B.8","5B.10","6B.1","6B.2","6B.3","8B.1","8B.2","8B.3","8B.6","8B.7"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Statement made in January 2023 and refers mainly to the government’s prior 14 years and future plans; outcomes are presented as Hasina’s claims.","ruler_attribution":"Hasina, as prime minister and Awami League president, made the claims and described government priorities.","limitations":["The report does not provide independent outcome data, budget execution evidence, or evidence that corruption reports led to remedies."]},{"source_id":"SRC-91c747e618a6752e","start_unit":1,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"During the June 25, 2023 budget debate, Hasina said the Awami League needed to remain in power to achieve Bangladesh’s 2026 development graduation and described poverty reduction, a reported 3% unemployment rate, economic self-reliance, and continued development as government goals. She defended the FY2023-24 Tk761,785-crore budget, said the deficit was kept within 5%, described responses to inflation, proposed a universal pension scheme, and instructed consideration of a 5% special allowance for government employees amid COVID-19 and Russia-Ukraine effects.","question_ids":["4B.2","4B.8","5B.1","5B.3","5B.6","5B.8","5B.9","5B.10","6B.1","6B.2","6B.6","6B.9","8B.1","8B.2","8B.3","8B.6","8B.7","8B.9","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly concerns the 2023-24 budget and 2023 statements, with some claims about longer-term performance and future intentions.","ruler_attribution":"Hasina presented the government’s program, budget position, crisis response and administrative instructions in parliament.","limitations":["The article does not independently verify the unemployment, poverty, deficit, inflation-control, or budget-implementation claims; the pension scheme was described as expected, not completed."]},{"source_id":"SRC-714c7aa200e7ebe4","start_unit":7,"end_unit":8,"fact_summary":"At the December 20, 2023 election campaign launch, Hasina urged voters to elect Awami League candidates so they could continue serving the public and pursuing a poverty-free developed Bangladesh. She described BNP and Jamaat as seeking to obstruct the January 7 election through arson and characterized BNP leaders as looters, killers, corrupt and embezzlers, while asking the public to resist what she called arson terrorism.","question_ids":["3B.3","3B.8","3B.9","4B.1","4B.2","4B.3","4B.6","4B.7","4B.9","5B.1","8B.1","8B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly concerns campaign rhetoric and the scheduled January 7, 2024 election, during the 2023 campaign period.","ruler_attribution":"Hasina, as prime minister and Awami League leader, made the appeal and accusations at a party-organized public rally.","limitations":["The report does not independently establish the accuracy of the accusations, the extent of opposition violence, or whether the rhetoric caused harm."]},{"source_id":"SRC-e26da6a53577c7fa","start_unit":7,"end_unit":7,"fact_summary":"At a March 11, 2023 rally, Hasina accused BNP leaders of lying, corruption and looting, defended her government by citing 103 development projects in Mymensingh, and formally inaugurated 73 projects worth Tk570.07 crore while laying foundation stones for 30 schemes worth Tk2,762.27 crore.","question_ids":["3B.3","4B.3","5B.1","5B.6","5B.7","8B.1","8B.2","8B.3","8B.6","8B.7"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly concerns March 2023 rhetoric and project inaugurations.","ruler_attribution":"Hasina made the accusations and inaugurated or announced the projects as prime minister at an Awami League rally.","limitations":["The report does not assess project completion, procurement integrity, outcomes, or the truth of the accusations and development claims."]},{"source_id":"SRC-07985b7f5bb606f4","start_unit":7,"end_unit":8,"fact_summary":"In September 2023, Bangladesh’s foreign minister stated at the UN that Bangladesh supported eliminating nuclear weapons, remained committed to the Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons, urged implementation by all states, highlighted intentional and accidental-use risks, called for controls against unauthorized access, and urged renewed disarmament negotiations and peaceful nuclear technology research.","question_ids":["1B.1","1B.2","1B.4","1B.6","1B.8","1B.10"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Directly concerns Bangladesh’s stated position at a September 2023 UN meeting; the source attributes the statements to the foreign minister rather than Hasina personally.","ruler_attribution":"Bangladesh’s foreign minister articulated the government’s position; direct personal direction by Hasina is not shown.","limitations":["No evidence here of Hasina’s personal involvement, domestic implementation, funding, command-and-control safeguards, or measurable change in nuclear-risk posture."]},{"source_id":"SRC-37fbb51b21b6d013","start_unit":6,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"On April 10, 2023, Hasina told parliament that Prothom Alo was an enemy of the Awami League, democracy and the people, accused it of publishing a child’s allegedly induced false statement, and said it did not want stability. She also criticized the United States and unnamed actors over corruption, human rights and support for convicted persons.","question_ids":["3B.3","3B.8","4B.3","4B.6","4B.9","7B.1","7B.2","8B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly concerns Hasina’s April 2023 parliamentary speech.","ruler_attribution":"Hasina made the statements as prime minister and leader of the House.","limitations":["The report does not establish whether the newspaper’s account was false, whether state action followed, or whether the statements affected press freedom."]},{"source_id":"SRC-f33237d277164c51","start_unit":7,"end_unit":8,"fact_summary":"On April 10, 2023, Hasina again characterized Prothom Alo as an enemy of the Awami League, democracy and the people, alleging that it induced a seven-year-old to make a false statement. She also accused unnamed individuals of laundering money and attempting to destroy democracy, and criticized US statements on corruption and human rights.","question_ids":["3B.3","3B.8","4B.3","4B.6","4B.9","7B.1","7B.2","8B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly concerns the April 2023 parliamentary speech; this is a separately reported account of the same event as SRC-37fbb51b21b6d013.","ruler_attribution":"Hasina made the statements in parliament as prime minister.","limitations":["The report does not independently verify the allegations or document resulting legal, regulatory, or coercive action."]},{"source_id":"SRC-d3e22389604fe11d","start_unit":7,"end_unit":8,"fact_summary":"On January 25, 2023, Hasina told parliament that critics should identify her failures and said she would correct them; she attributed improvements for grassroots people to her government. She also said pandemic and Russia-Ukraine effects had raised prices and stated that the government established textile universities and colleges because the garment sector lacked technical workers.","question_ids":["5B.7","5B.9","5B.10","6B.2","6B.5","6B.6","8B.2","8B.4","8B.6","8B.7","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly concerns January 2023 parliamentary statements and reported education capacity measures; some welfare claims refer to the preceding 14 years.","ruler_attribution":"Hasina made the accountability invitation, crisis explanation, and education-policy claim as prime minister.","limitations":["No documented correction, audit, independent evaluation, or evidence of outcomes is provided."]},{"source_id":"SRC-9f9e29a3634f320a","start_unit":6,"end_unit":7,"fact_summary":"A BIISS proceedings publication dated October 25, 2023 described the Rohingya repatriation situation as diplomatically stalled with limited progress despite repeated attempts. Its overview recommended continued engagement with Myanmar and multilateral pressure, stronger atrocity documentation, improved camp services, host-community support, contingency planning, and repatriation that is safe, voluntary and dignified.","question_ids":["2B.1","2B.7","2B.9","2B.10","3B.7","3B.9","3B.10","6B.2","6B.3","6B.6","6B.10","8B.8","8B.9","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly concerns the Rohingya policy environment and recommendations in October 2023, but describes a policy discussion rather than a verified decision by Hasina.","ruler_attribution":"The publication records institutional and expert discussion in Bangladesh; it does not attribute the recommendations or implementation directly to Hasina.","limitations":["No direct evidence here of Hasina’s specific orders, funding, implementation, or responsibility for the reported stalemate."]},{"source_id":"SRC-8ada9286565ea78f","start_unit":2,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"On November 1, 2023, Saima Wazed, Hasina’s daughter, was nominated by WHO South-East Asia member states as regional director for a five-year term beginning in 2024 after receiving 8 of 10 votes. The report described Wazed’s mental-health, autism and public-health experience and noted her existing advisory and academic roles.","question_ids":["6B.3","6B.4","6B.9","7B.5"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly concerns a November 2023 election and appointment taking effect in 2024.","ruler_attribution":"The source identifies Wazed as Hasina’s daughter but does not report Hasina’s role in the nomination or vote.","limitations":["The document does not establish nepotism, government interference, or Hasina’s involvement in the appointment process."]},{"source_id":"SRC-c5ed334db10d3e7d","start_unit":3,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"A November 2, 2023 report said WHO selected Hasina’s daughter, Saima Wazed, as South-East Asia regional director after she had rejected allegations that she used her mother’s influence; it also reported that The Lancet had raised transparency and nepotism concerns because other candidates had medical or doctoral credentials and noted her honorary doctorate.","question_ids":["6B.4","6B.9","7B.3","7B.5","7B.6","7B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly concerns the November 2023 selection and contemporaneous criticism.","ruler_attribution":"The report links the appointment controversy to Hasina through the familial relationship, but provides no evidence that Hasina directed or benefited from the selection.","limitations":["The allegations are reported criticisms, not adjudicated findings; the source does not document Hasina’s conduct or the selection process beyond the reported concerns."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":[],"batch_limitations":["The supplied sources are predominantly contemporaneous news reports of official statements and claims; they provide limited independent verification of outcomes, implementation, institutional safeguards, or Hasina’s personal responsibility for actions attributed to ministers, officials, or institutions."]}
